# UCSC kent source inventory

Repository: [ucscGenomeBrowser/kent](https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent)  
Inspected revision: `ad6dd2177ad20bea9e32563ee76a1c598bccb6d5` (resolved by the runner through the GitHub commits API before launch).  
Retrieval date: 2026-09-30. The tree API reported `truncated: false`.

## Repository scope and uses

The repository README describes a broad source tree for UCSC Genome Browser biological analysis and web display programs, command-line tools, and supporting libraries. It distinguishes this tree from the smaller MIT-licensed `kent-core` subset and notes that browser data, assembly databases, and large `/gbdb` assets are distributed separately. The inspected areas support assembly coordinate remapping, genomic signal aggregation over intervals, filtering variant data, and querying/exporting hosted genome-browser tracks. These are source-backed capabilities, not verified task executions.

Seven units are recorded in `units.jsonl`: `kent-liftover-annotation-remapping`, `kent-bigwig-region-signal-summary`, `kent-vcffilter-allele-count-filter`, `kent-table-browser-track-query-export`, `kent-two-bit-reference-sequence-extraction`, `kent-custom-track-upload-and-visual-check`, and `kent-genepred-to-bed-annotation-conversion`. Two support/data records are in `datasets.jsonl`: `kent-vcffilter-sarscov2-fixture` and the candidate reference product `kent-hg38-twobit-reference`. No other dataset record was justified by inspected sources. In particular, the bigWig command has no named study input; the Table Browser tutorial gives generic track examples without pinning track versions; and liftOver needs caller-supplied assembly-specific annotations and chain files.

## Source map and inspection queue

| Collection/location | Status and records | Remaining leads |
|---|---|---|
| Repository overview: `README` | Inspected; establishes repository purpose, source/data split, licensing caveat, and install entry points. | Detailed `LICENSE` terms and subdirectory-specific terms remain to inspect before any reuse decision. |
| User tutorials: `docs/tutorials/` | Partially inspected: `tableBrowserTutorial.md` and `customTrackTutorial.md` inspected and recorded as `kent-table-browser-track-query-export` and `kent-custom-track-upload-and-visual-check`; `gb101.md` skimmed for genome browser tools and search context. | `gatewayTutorial.md`, tutorial index, and full `gb101.md` remain pending. The Table Browser tutorial's later output/download sections were not exhaustively read. |
| Assembly remapping docs and implementation: `src/hg/doc/liftOver.txt`, `src/hg/liftOver/liftOver.c` | Inspected; `kent-liftover-annotation-remapping`. Also inspected source usage, format branches, chain direction, output files, flags, caveats, and documented chain-building / genePred example. | `src/hg/liftOver/README.txt`, liftOver test makefile and fixture coverage, `liftOverMerge`, hub/API liftOver, and assembly-specific chain and annotation sources remain pending. |
| Signal aggregation utility: `src/utils/bigWigAverageOverBed/` | Partially inspected: main C implementation/usage; `kent-bigwig-region-signal-summary`. | Utility makefile/tests, expected outputs, docs, and candidate bigWig/region examples remain pending. |
| VCF utility and fixtures: `src/utils/vcfFilter/` | Partially inspected: implementation, tests makefile, bounded view of `tests/input/subset.vcf`, and `tests/expected/testMinAc1Gt.vcf`; recorded as `kent-vcffilter-allele-count-filter` and dataset `kent-vcffilter-sarscov2-fixture`. | Exclusion fixture content, remaining expected fixtures, upstream aligned FASTA / `faToVcf` preparation, provenance of labeled samples, and source terms remain pending. |
| Sequence and annotation utilities: `src/utils/`, `src/hg/` | Partially inspected: `twoBitToFa/twoBitToFa.c` and its makefile regression command list; unit `kent-two-bit-reference-sequence-extraction`. Also read the `bedGraphToBigWig` usage/test makefile, but deferred it as a format-preparation utility rather than a distinct scientific operation. | `faToTwoBit`, `genePredToBed`, interval operations, and other commands found by tree path inventory remain pending. |
| Browser tracks, downloads, and documentation: `docs/`, `src/hg/makeDb/trackDb/`, external UCSC data pages | Tutorials inspected above; `twoBitToFa` usage names hg38 `latest/hg38.2bit`, recorded with unknown version/terms as `kent-hg38-twobit-reference`. | No actual assembly content, track accession/version, study or paper was inspected. Search track docs and UCSC data pages for named studies and pin an immutable data version if useful. |

## Evidence and boundaries

- The liftOver source accepts BED by default and additional annotation formats, writes mapped and unmapped outputs, expects the old genome on the chain target and the new genome on the query, and warns that cross-species mappings are not designed as homology answers. `src/hg/doc/liftOver.txt` labels its procedure untested; its historical cluster example is not execution evidence.
- The signal utility source defines the separate `mean0` and covered-base `mean`, supports BED12 blocks and optional center sampling/min-max/statistics, and checks BED names for uniqueness. No command was run.
- The VCF fixture header says `VCFv4.2`, reference `NC_045512v2`, and source `faToVcf refPlus.unmapped.aligned.fasta stdout`; sample labels look like dated SARS-CoV-2 sample metadata. The original biological study, exact source observations, complete input-generation chain, and redistribution terms are unknown. A second exclusion file appears in the test makefile but was not inspected; it is listed as a separate support asset only because the tree identifies it as a distinct test input, not as a separate dataset.
- The Table Browser tutorial describes selecting a genome/assembly, track/table, region, filters/intersections, and output. It gives examples of SNP overlap with RefSeq coding exons and regions overlapping a peak track, but no pinned result or exact data version.
- `twoBitToFa` source documents the hg38 `latest` URL and supports zero-based half-open fragments and BED extraction; code concatenates BED blocks, omits introns, and reverse-complements negative-strand records. Its tiny bundled test twoBit files are format fixtures rather than identified biological data.
- `genePredToBed` converts gene model spans/CDS/strand/exon arrays to BED12 blocks and explicitly does not yet handle genePredExt; recorded as `kent-genepred-to-bed-annotation-conversion`. Its test makefile points to a regression fixture, but that fixture was not inspected.
- The Custom Track tutorial describes display and hosted-file requirements; custom-track data are described as temporary. It contributes a visualization workflow, not evidence for quantitative validation.
- These candidate workflows may support artifact-grading tasks (e.g., mapped/unmapped coordinate tables, interval-level signal summaries, transformed VCF, or selected track records). Deterministic grading, runtime, data rights, and real-world scientific suitability remain unresolved and need authoring/validation.

## Deduplication and stopping state

Related command implementation and usage documentation are represented by one liftOver unit. Repeated VCF regression outputs are treated as evidence for one filtering operation, and the input VCF is one fixture dataset rather than multiple datasets per test case. The Table Browser's separate interface steps compose one query/export workflow. Tutorial screenshots and interactive pages are not separate units because inspected text presents them as alternative media for the same workflow.

The pass remains partial and stopped at the supplied 15:09:19 UTC deadline after inspecting the final mapped command entry and validating inventory structure. The selected source requests succeeded; some jq filtering attempts returned syntax errors, then a corrected tree query completed and reported an untruncated tree. Remaining leads include `gatewayTutorial.md`, `faToTwoBit`, interval operations, utility regression fixture contents, and the provenance/terms for the sample fixture and hg38 reference asset. No build, scientific tool, or pipeline was executed.
